attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his Substack post, stated in his own voice.

semantics.note: Faithful to his account of the May 2023 testimony. It leaves out the 'loved his job' element, but that adds nothing material.

contract.note: Reading 'lied by omission' as knowingly creating a misleading impression is the ordinary reading. Separating direct equity from indirect interests, and control from profit rights, is fair. The result depends on whether the omission was knowing.

evidence.note: The official transcript confirms 'no equity in OpenAI' and 'doing this because I love it', with no indirect interest mentioned.

OpenAI's own disclosure admits an indirect YC-fund interest dating from before he was full-time, so it existed at the hearing. It also says he held no direct equity, so his literal words were accurate.
Reporting, confirmed by the company, says Altman was the fund's named controller from 2021, which plausibly covers the hearing date. It says nothing on whether he profited.
Reuters reports his ownership but quotes OpenAI saying he had no financial interest in the fund. This weakens the economic-stake reading. It is the company's claim, not an independent finding.

reviews.rationale: Supported: the testimony matches his quote, and the omitted interests (an indirect YC-fund stake, and named control of the Startup Fund) appear to have existed at the hearing. Not settled: whether Altman knowingly misled. His words were literally true for direct equity, and OpenAI says he had no financial interest in the fund. The contract's condition for knowing deception is not met, and nothing contradicts the factual parts.

attribution.note: Marcus's own closing sentence in his post.

semantics.note: The paraphrase is fair. 'Seeming less and less on the level' is an impression, and the power trend has no baseline. The statement is mostly evaluative commentary.

contract.note: The contract rightly declines to turn 'seeming' into a firm claim of dishonesty and notes there is no baseline for power, so it has no testable truth condition.

evidence.note: Altman's March 2024 return to the board shows more formal authority. It is not a measure of the trend he describes or of honesty.
Altman joined the safety committee on May 28, 2024. Membership alone does not show consolidation and says nothing on honesty.

reviews.rationale: The sentence pairs a power trend with no baseline and an explicitly qualified impression ('seeming') of declining honesty. Governance records give partial context on authority, but no objective criterion can confirm or refute the combined statement.
